Use text-to-speech if you can't proofread aloud
by Evan Hahn, updated Feb 1, 2025 (originally posted Mar 25, 2011), tagged #writing #productivity

In short: Use text-to-speech to read your writing back to you if you can’t proofread it out loud.

I often find it useful to proofread by reading aloud. When I speak, I’m more aware of awkward wording and grammar errors. I like to read my writing aloud before I publish a blog post, or write an important email, or send a cover letter.

However, sometimes I’m not in a quiet place. When I’m in public, I don’t want to be belting my writing out to everyone.

In cases like these, you can use text-to-speech software to hear your essay through your headphones. I’ve found this to be an effective alternative to reading aloud!
